The ghost of every gag is printed faintly on the glass and lights when its turn comes: she sips a coconut while a ship crosses the horizon behind her; a bottle goes out to sea and washes straight back to her feet; a drone lowers a parcel that opens to reveal another pair of headphones; a shark fin wearing headphones tilts on the beat; a cat drifts in on a crate; she holds her phone up and one signal bar lights at the top of the palm; a sea turtle dozes beside her, Z by Z; a coconut drops on a hermit crab, which walks off wearing it. <h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours of island, tuned to 80 BPM. Signal: one bar, top of the palm.</b>
</p>

<p align="center">
  A stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the 10-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She idles, nodding to the music in her headphones, and every so often something happens. Mostly, it does not. That is the point.<br>
  <sub>An unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 screensaver, and not affiliated with it or its owners. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p and 30 fps, and always daytime.</sub>
</p>

<p align="center">
  More than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-01) wait on four timers in <a href="activities.toml"><code>activities.toml</code></a>, from <i>regular</i> (every 2 to 5 minutes) to <i>super rare</i> (every 3 to 6 hours), and each one starts on the next bar of the music, so the gags land on the beat: a bottle that washes straight back, a drone that delivers another pair of headphones, a shark in headphones nodding along. Every sound is synthesized from code in <a href="tools/make_audio.py"><code>tools/make_audio.py</code></a>: no samples, no loops, no recordings.
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">
  <sub>Live preview in the browser, then one button for a YouTube-ready MP4. Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. In development: no video is out yet.<br>
  The banner is the display in shop <b>DEMO</b> mode, which packs a few hours of gags into sixty seconds. The real thing spreads them over ten hours and leaves the <b>IDLE</b> lamp on in between.</sub>
</p>

<details>
<summary><b>LAMP TEST</b>: what every light on the panel means</summary>

```text
 IDLETRONIC IR-600 · DISPLAY LEGEND
 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 LAMP         MEANS                                        LIT
 DEMO         shop demo: a few hours of gags in 60 s       blinking
 ▶ PLAY       the video is playing                         always
 REPEAT 1     the theme is a seamless 60 s loop            always
 ♪            the beat: 80 BPM, one every 0.75 s           on the beat
 ST           stereo                                       always
 IDLE         she idles, nodding to the music              most of it
 BUSY         she is doing something                       about 1/3
 DAYTIME      it is daytime                                always
 NIGHT        it is night                                  never
 SYNTH        every sound is synthesized from code         always
 SAMPLES      a sound came from a recording                never
 TIME 0:00    time into the 60 s theme loop                counting
 TUNED 80.0   tempo, in BPM (F major, ii-V-I-vi)           always
 BAR 01/20    bar of the theme: 20 bars of 3 s             counting
 REGULAR      this gag came off the 2 to 5 min timer       per gag
 OCCASIONAL   this gag came off the 12 to 25 min timer     per gag
 RARE         this gag came off the 30 to 60 min timer     per gag
 SUPER RARE   this gag came off the 3 to 6 h timer         not today
 LEVEL        drums, e.piano, kalimba, vinyl, surf: L, R   bouncing
 ISLAND       every gag is printed on the glass, faintly,  in turn
              and lights up when its timer comes round
```

The NIGHT lamp is not broken. The island is always daytime: that is a project rule, so the lamp is there for completeness and nothing else.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>DEMO MODE</b>: the sixty-second loop, bar by bar</summary>

```text
 DEMO MODE · 20 BARS OF 3 S · 60 S · THEN AGAIN
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 BAR    TICKER          ON THE ISLAND                         SHE   TIMER
 01-02  CASTAWAY        nodding on every beat, notes lit      IDLE  ·
 03     LO-FI ISLAND    nodding                               IDLE  ·
 04     TEN HOURS       nodding                               IDLE  ·
 05     SHE IDLES       nodding                               IDLE  ·
 06     MOSTLY.         nodding                               IDLE  ·
 07     COCONUT SIP     she sips; a ship crosses behind her   BUSY  REGULAR
 08     BOTTLE BACK     out to sea, straight back to her      BUSY  OCCAS.
 09     DRONE DROP      a parcel is lowered onto the sand     BUSY  RARE
 10     HEADPHONES?     it is another pair of headphones      BUSY  RARE
 11     SHARK NODS      a fin in headphones, on the beat      IDLE  RARE
 12     CAT ON CRATE    a stray cat drifts in on a crate      IDLE  RARE
 13     ONE BAR         phone up: one bar, top of the palm    BUSY  RARE
 14     TURTLE NAP      a turtle visits; they both doze off   BUSY  OCCAS.
 15     BONK            crab gets a coconut, walks off in it  BUSY  OCCAS.
 16     NO SAMPLES      nodding                               IDLE  ·
 17     ALL CODE        nodding                               IDLE  ·
 18     RUN SERVE.PY    nodding                               IDLE  ·
 19     127.0.0.1:8765  nodding                               IDLE  ·
 20     WAIT FOR IT     lamp test, left to right, then 01     IDLE  ·
```

Every message lands exactly on a bar line, like the gags do: in the video, every activity waits for the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds. The ship in bar 07 is on its own lane, so it can sail past while she is busy with a coconut. Busy for 7 bars out of 20, which is a little over a third, which is about right.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>SPECIFICATIONS</b>: the IR-600 spec sheet, with real numbers</summary>

```text
 IDLETRONIC IR-600 · TEN-HOUR STEREO ISLAND RECEIVER · SPECIFICATIONS
 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 PROGRAMME ....... one island, one tall palm, one raft, one young woman
                   in cream headphones. stationary frame, always daytime
 PICTURE ......... 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, made for YouTube
 RUN LENGTH ...... 10:00:00 by default, seed 1992: same seed, same video
 TUNING .......... 80 BPM, F major, ii-V-I-vi, 20 bars of exactly 3 s
 PROGRAMMES ...... more than 90 activities (94 on 2026-10-01): most on
                   four timers, the rest chained follow-ups
 TIMERS .......... per 10 h, median of 200 simulated runs:
   REGULAR         every 2 to 5 min       about 155
   OCCASIONAL      every 12 to 25 min     about 30
   RARE            every 30 to 60 min     about 13
   SUPER RARE      every 3 to 6 h         about 2 (3 at most)
 SNAP TO BAR ..... every activity starts on the next bar (3 s)
 LANES ........... hers, plus the cat's, the turtle's, the sea and sky's
                   and the shore's, so things can overlap
 DUTY CYCLE ...... busy about a third of the time, idle the rest
 SOUND ........... more than 150 files, every one synthesized from code:
                   no samples, no loops, no recordings
 THEME ........... seamless 60 s loop: electric piano, kalimba lead,
                   soft drums, vinyl crackle
 AMBIENCE ........ ocean, also a seamless 60 s loop
 MASTER .......... -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP; levels set
                   in master and per routine
 OUTPUT .......... frame-exact export in the browser (WebCodecs H.264,
                   68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome); the
                   server mixes the sound and joins it into an MP4
 BUILD STEP ...... none. plain ES modules, no npm packages
 MODEL NUMBER .... 600, as in minutes
 LISTENED TO ..... not yet, by anyone
```

Where the numbers live: the timers in [activities.toml](activities.toml), which [tools/schedule.py](tools/schedule.py) checks before simulating a ten-hour run (`python tools/schedule.py`). The sound comes from [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py). The renderer is [a web page](web/index.html) served by [tools/serve.py](tools/serve.py); [tools/render_demo.py](tools/render_demo.py) is the older Python reference renderer, and `python tools/render_demo.py --dev` makes a dev reel of every activity with a heads-up display. The working notes are in [MUSING.md](MUSING.md).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>TROUBLESHOOTING</b>: before you call the island</summary>

- **The NIGHT lamp will not light.** Correct. It is always daytime on the island. That is a rule, not a fault.
- **The SAMPLES lamp will not light.** Correct. Every sound is generated by code. There is nothing to sample.
- **SUPER RARE never lights.** Leave the unit on. That timer goes off every 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 times a run, and the demo lasts one minute.
- **The display said BONK.** A coconut fell on a hermit crab. The crab is fine. The crab is wearing the coconut now.
- **It only ever says ONE BAR.** That is the signal. It is at the top of the palm. She has checked.
- **The buttons on the picture do nothing.** They are a picture. The working ones are in the web page: `python tools/serve.py`, then http://127.0.0.1:8765/.
- **There is no sound.** GitHub keeps sound out of READMEs. Nobody has heard the soundtrack yet anyway, including the code that wrote it.
- **Nothing is happening.** Correct. Wait for it.

<sub>The IDLETRONIC IR-600, its maker and its model number are invented for this README; no real receiver was opened. The panel is drawn by a script: 16-segment and 7-segment cells, an original stroke font, no fonts, no bitmaps. The island is original too.</sub>

</details>
